1.notes: One claim: a controlled prop change made during blur handling in onBlur mode goes through validation.change -> commit(value, true) and publishes all-valid over the blur verdict. The generalisation to any programmatic change on an invalid field is the same mechanism and is not split. The NumberFieldInput comparison is inventoried as a corrective request.

claims.quote: takes the revalidate path and publishes all-valid, wiping an error that blur validation just set
claims.notes: Obligation: onBlur validation must leave the validator's verdict for the settled value. Mechanism traced in source: blur commits and publishes the error; the consumer's trim changes the value prop; useValueChanged calls validation.change, which in onBlur mode calls commit(value, true); with state.valid === false and no valueMissing it calls publishAllValid without running validate. Consequence: an invalid field reports valid after the user leaves it. At merge-base no path reacted to the prop change, so the error stayed. Same trigger, mechanism and consequence as GT-r1 (sync half). Not rerun: the run tool refused vitest execution.
evidence: clone/packages/react/src/field/root/useFieldValidation.ts: change() calls commit(value, !validateOnChange); revalidate branch returns unless state.valid === false, then publishAllValid when valueMissing is false.
git diff 30b8ea20..14d39e5d on FieldControl.tsx: merge-base had no value-prop sync path.
clone/packages/react/src/field/root/FieldRoot.tsx JSDoc: onBlur triggers validation when the control loses focus.

2.notes: One claim: programmatic reset to empty after a submit attempt runs full validation and shows a required error. Novel; no family covers it.

claims.quote: Resetting a controlled field from code after a submit attempt now runs full validation on the reset value, so a freshly cleared form shows required errors.
claims.notes: Source supports the mechanism: Form sets submitAttemptedRef true on submit and never resets it; shouldValidateOnChange() is then true in onSubmit mode; the reset to '' fires useValueChanged -> validation.change('') -> full commit; markedDirtyRef is true, so valueMissing is published as invalid. Merge-base had no reaction to a prop change. Disputed because the PR intends programmatic changes to sync validity and the JSDoc says onSubmit re-validates on change after submission, yet a required error on a just-reset form after a successful submit is a visible regression for the reset case the PR cites. Needs a ruling. Not rerun: execution refused.
evidence: clone/packages/react/src/form/Form.tsx onSubmit: submitAttemptedRef.current = true, never cleared; onFormSubmit called after validation passes.
clone/packages/react/src/field/root/useFieldValidation.ts getState: valueMissing counts once markedDirtyRef is true.

3.notes: One claim: programmatic (async-loaded) values mark dirty against the mount baseline and validate in onChange mode.

claims.quote: Any programmatic value change is compared against the mount-time baseline, so values loaded asynchronously mark the field dirty
claims.notes: The behaviour is accurate and new at head, but it is the PR's stated and tested contract: the added test 'syncs state and validates when the controlled value changes programmatically' asserts data-dirty and one validate call after a programmatic setValue in onChange mode. It also matches the documented meaning of dirty (changed from initial value) and of onChange mode (every change). The single-capture baseline is pre-existing and documented in useFieldControlRegistration. A fair design caution for async-loaded forms, below the correction threshold. Not rerun.

4.notes: One claim: registering the serialized value changes the type validate receives on submit and the public initialValue.

claims.quote: Registering the serialized value changes what `validate` receives on submit and `actionsRef.validate()`
claims.notes: Source supports it: the registration's value feeds getRegistrationValue, which the field's validate() (Form submit and actionsRef) passes to commit and which captureInitialValue stores. 5.notes: One claim covering both variants (preventBaseUIHandler and a prevented native event) in controlled mode.

claims.quote: no longer suppress dirty, clearErrors, or validation
claims.notes: Accurate from source: the controlled branch returns before the defaultPrevented guard and the sync runs from the prop. In both scenarios the consumer still sets the new value, so the field state then describes the value actually shown; the merge-base result left state stale against it. The PR states that the value prop owns the controlled path. Native input and change events on text inputs are not cancelable, so the prevented variant depends on synthetic events; no browser was available to check further. No concrete harm established.
